title: ERIS vs Salesforce: which one fits your company?
content_html:
ERIS vs Salesforce comes down to two different jobs. Salesforce is an AI CRM that, according to its website, connects a company's customer data, apps and AI agents on one platform for businesses of every size, and it offers a free way to get started. ERIS from Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is in beta now. It is one system that replaces a company's separate business tools, with an AI assistant that always runs on a local AI model, either on the company's own servers or on Upward's own servers in the Netherlands. If you only want a CRM with AI agents, Salesforce fits that specialty. If you need company data kept away from outside AI providers and one system for the whole business, pick ERIS.

Status of ERIS: ERIS is in beta now, with design partners. New apps arrive almost every week.

What Salesforce is good at

Salesforce is a CRM a sales team can use today, and its website describes a broad platform around it. All points below are from its website, read in November 2026.

  • AI CRM. Salesforce describes itself as an AI CRM. It helps organisations connect with customers by linking the data, apps and agents that keep the business running.
  • One platform. It says it brings people, agents, apps and data together on one platform.
  • Any size, any sector. It says small and large customers in every sector use it, and that it delivers value for businesses of every size.
  • AI agents with IT controls. Agentforce gives IT security controls, monitoring and management tools for scaling AI across the organisation.
  • Agents in Slack. Salesforce agents work inside Slack, where people ask questions and agents take action.
  • Flexible buying. Agentforce can be bought with usage-based pricing or with per-user licences. Usage-based pricing means paying per action with Flex Credits, or paying per conversation. Detailed pricing comes from a Salesforce sales representative.
  • Easy start. Salesforce offers a free way to get started.

For a company whose main need is a CRM with AI agents, these are real strengths.

What ERIS does differently

ERIS is not a CRM first. It is one system for the business tools a company runs on, with AI agents that work across all apps on the company's own data.

Wider scope than sales. What ERIS includes:

  • Meetings, meeting notes and the note taker, and the task manager.
  • Project management, document management, document signing, CRM, bookkeeping, tax and procurement, standards (ISO 27001 and NIS2, the EU cybersecurity rules), pipeline, quotes and outreach, and content and social media.
  • Finance, HR, support and legal.
  • The main portal with the ERIS Assistant, team chat and email.

Where it runs. ERIS has two deployment options:

  • On the company's own servers. With this option the data never leaves the building.
  • Hosted for you by a cloud or telecom provider, also as a private cloud at a European provider. This option is for companies without their own hardware.

Both options always use a local AI model. No outside AI provider receives client data in either option. More on this approach is in how on-premises AI keeps enterprise data inside the firewall.

An assistant that only sees what you may see. The ERIS Assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. A refused access is logged like every other question.

A log of every AI action. Every question and every AI action is logged: who asked, which data was used, what the assistant did and the result.

Instructions in documents are treated as content. The assistant reads instructions inside an email or document as content, never as commands to follow. This lowers the risk of prompt injection (hidden text that tries to steer an AI).

A simple price model. ERIS is priced as one licence and one price per user. On the on-premise option the company owns the hardware the AI runs on, so the AI is not billed per action. That hardware still costs money to buy, maintain and update.

One step at a time. A company replaces its software app by app, at its own pace.

Local AI has real costs. It needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU (graphics processing unit) server. Its speed depends on that hardware. It reads and searches company documents and is not trained on them. The guide to running a local AI assistant on company documents explains what that takes.

Which one should you pick

Salesforce fits if you only want a CRM. It offers a free way to start and is focused on sales.

Salesforce fits if your team already works in Slack and wants AI agents there. Its website says Salesforce agents work inside Slack.

Salesforce fits if you want to pay for AI by use. Agentforce offers per-action and per-conversation pricing as well as per-user licences.

Pick ERIS if company data may not go to outside AI providers. This suits companies that cannot or will not send data out because of GDPR (the EU data protection rules), the EU AI Act (the EU law on AI) or NIS2. Whether a deployment meets those rules depends on the use case and is assessed per deployment. Whatever you choose, check the vendor's terms on how customer data is handled.

Pick ERIS if you want sales, documents, bookkeeping and tasks in one system. ERIS replaces a stack of separate tools rather than only the CRM, and new apps arrive almost every week. If the wider choice of all-in-one systems interests you, see the overview of all-in-one business software. For a similar comparison with another large vendor, read ERIS vs Microsoft 365 Copilot.

FAQ

Do I need my own IT team to run ERIS?

Not necessarily. ERIS runs on the company's own hardware with a local AI model, or hosted for you by a cloud or telecom provider, also as a private cloud at a European provider. A company without its own IT team can choose the hosted option. Running ERIS on your own premises costs hardware, maintenance and updates. Upward Technologies also offers hosting and support.

What hardware does ERIS need?

Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU server. Its speed depends on that hardware, and existing servers are not always enough. A company that does not want to run its own hardware can use the hosted option on Upward's own servers in the Netherlands.

Can ERIS connect to the software we already use?

Custom apps, agents and knowledge bases are built for a company as projects and billed separately. Upward Technologies also builds ERP and CRM integrations. For a specific connection, for example to Salesforce, ask Upward Technologies directly.

How many employees does ERIS suit?

ERIS is made for whole companies, from small teams to large organisations. It runs for the whole company, not for one person on a single computer. Access is set per person. The ERIS Assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open.
